humanoid_clip_mesh — DRIVE humanoid op

• Data kinds: table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.humanoid_clip_mesh(clip: 'dict', distance: 'float') -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import drivehumanoid; drivehumanoid.humanoid_clip_mesh(clip: 'dict', distance: 'float') -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("humanoid_clip_mesh"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Mesh at walked distance distance [m] ({"V","F","color","label","dims"}, origin = directly below the hips, +x = forward).

One cycle advances cycle_length. Between frames the vertices are interpolated linearly (the face connectivity is the same in all frames). The shape keeps its origin directly below the hips, so if you advance the placement position by distance, the stance foot appears to stay still on the ground (the frame phase is matched to the distance walked in advance). ★2026-10-03: the first version also subtracted the forward progress within the cycle here, subtracting it twice together with the placing side (caught by the sliding gate).

Empty input (clip is an empty dict) raises ValueError.
